document.title: Know when an HTML report is ready to share
document.summary: One validation result combines visual, functional, and declared-browser evidence without treating missing checks as success.
document.reviewFocus: Does this define enough observable evidence for an author to decide whether a generated report is ready to share, without prescribing the validator's implementation?
sources: User request on 26 Jul 2026: create a PRD for testing generated HTML reports before sharing, with visual, functional, and cross-browser acceptance criteria.
No product interface or browser support matrix was supplied; interface shape remains a design concern and the browser matrix remains an owned product decision.

sections.title: A report can look finished while critical review states remain broken
sections.summary: An author has one self-contained HTML artifact and needs evidence strong enough to make a sharing decision.

items: Moment
A report author has generated a self-contained HTML document and is preparing to share it with reviewers or stakeholders.
Friction
A report can appear correct in one browser while hiding clipped content, broken navigation, inaccessible controls, missing fallback behavior, or print defects.
Bet
Give the author one validation result that combines visual review, functional checks, and evidence from the declared browser matrix.
Proof
The author can distinguish ready, failed, and incomplete validation without interpreting build logs or assuming that an untested state passed.
Boundary
Validation determines readiness; it does not author, repair, approve, publish, or distribute the report.

sections.title: A convincing default view is not readiness evidence
sections.summary: Without explicit state and environment evidence, report authors can mistake omissions for success.

items: Visual defects can exist only at narrow, short-height, enlarged-text, or print states.
Keyboard, disclosure, internal-navigation, and fallback behavior can fail while the default desktop view looks correct.
One browser preview says nothing about a required browser or platform that was never run.
Raw logs and silent omissions force the author to infer the aggregate result.

sections.title: A report earns an explicit readiness result
sections.summary: The author never infers success from silence, partial execution, or a single browser preview.

items.title: Identify the artifact
items.text: Select the finished HTML report and the browser support matrix that applies to it.

items.title: Run required checks
items.text: Evaluate visual, functional, fallback, print, and browser states against the same immutable artifact.

items.title: Review evidence
items.text: Show every required check as passed, failed, or not run, with context sufficient to reproduce failures.

items.title: Decide readiness
items.text: Mark ready only when every mandatory check passes; keep failures and missing checks visible.

sections.title: Evidence flows from one immutable artifact to the sharing decision

blocks.question: How does a finished report earn a trustworthy readiness result?
blocks.caption: The validator owns evidence collection and classification; the author owns the sharing decision. The policy rail prevents not-run checks or evidence from another artifact from producing ready.
walkthrough: The author selects one finished report, establishing the artifact under review.
The validator evaluates all required states and records an explicit outcome for each.
The aggregate result is ready, failed, or incomplete and preserves the supporting evidence.
The result informs—but does not make or approve—the author's sharing decision.

sections.title: The author makes a defensible sharing decision from one result

blocks.title: Validate one finished report before distribution
blocks.outcome: The author can tell whether the exact report is ready, failed, or incomplete and can act on the unresolved evidence.
blocks.boundary: One finished self-contained HTML artifact and its declared browser matrix; generation, repair, approval, hosting, and distribution stay outside the slice.

story.capability: validate one finished report across all mandatory review states
story.outcome: I can decide whether to share it without interpreting raw build logs or assuming missing evidence passed

scenarios.title: All mandatory checks pass
scenarios.given: the author selects one immutable report and a complete declared browser matrix
scenarios.when: every required visual, functional, fallback, print, and browser check passes against that artifact
scenarios.then: the result identifies the artifact and matrix and reports ready with all category evidence visible

scenarios.title: A required state fails
scenarios.given: the selected report clips content at a required viewport or has broken keyboard operation
scenarios.then: the result reports failed, identifies the affected state, and gives enough context to reproduce the defect

scenarios.title: Required browser evidence is missing
scenarios.given: one browser or platform in the declared matrix is unavailable or omitted
scenarios.then: that environment is reported as not run and the overall result remains incomplete rather than ready

steps.title: Select
steps.context: The author has a finished report and an applicable support matrix.
steps.action: They submit the exact artifact and matrix for validation.
steps.response: The validator identifies both inputs and fixes them as the evidence boundary.
steps.outcome: Subsequent checks can be attributed to one artifact and one declared environment set.

steps.title: Evaluate
steps.action: Required visual, functional, fallback, print, and browser checks run.
steps.response: Each check records passed, failed, or not run with its review state and environment.
steps.outcome: Silence and unavailable environments cannot masquerade as success.

steps.title: Summarize
steps.action: The author opens the validation result.
steps.response: The result shows the artifact, validation time, matrix, category outcomes, and unresolved failures or skipped checks.
steps.outcome: The author understands both the aggregate state and the evidence behind it.

steps.title: Decide
steps.context: The result is ready, failed, or incomplete.
steps.action: The author decides whether to share or resolve the evidence gaps.
steps.response: Ready appears only when every mandatory check passed against the same artifact.
steps.outcome: The sharing decision is evidence-based and does not imply factual correctness, security, approval, or publication.

acceptance.text: A conforming report that passes every mandatory state in the declared matrix is reported as ready.
Clipped content, overlap, unreadable hierarchy, or unintended page-level overflow fails the affected viewport or print state.
Intentional wide figures retain readable text through documented overflow treatment rather than unsafe shrinking.
Status remains understandable without color alone and focus indicators remain visible.
Internal navigation, native disclosures, controls, keyboard focus order, and authored destinations work.
The report loads as a self-contained file without remote fonts, styles, scripts, images, frames, or services.
No-JavaScript, script-stripped, reduced-motion, and print states preserve every primary fact, conclusion, warning, source, and next action.
Each browser result names browser, version, platform, and state; omitted required environments are not run, never passed.
A ready result is impossible while any required check has failed or not run.
A rerun evaluates the current artifact and does not present prior success as evidence for changed HTML.
The final result identifies the artifact, validation time, declared matrix, category outcomes, and unresolved failures or skipped checks.

blocks.after: The author either shares a ready artifact or returns to the report workflow with named failures and missing evidence; validation itself performs no repair or approval.

sections.title: Validate one finished report before distribution

items: In scope
One finished self-contained HTML report; visual, functional, accessibility-fallback, print, and declared-browser evidence; a readiness summary with failures and missing checks.
Out of scope
Report generation, content editing, automatic repair, approval workflow, hosting, distribution, factual accuracy, security, privacy, regulatory compliance, and undeclared browser environments.
Every required check exposes passed, failed, or not run.
Ready requires all mandatory checks to pass against the same report artifact.
A failed result identifies the affected review state and provides reproducible context.
A rerun evaluates the current artifact; prior success is not evidence for changed HTML.
The validator never claims that content is factually correct, secure, approved, or published.

sections.title: The author can make a defensible sharing decision

items: A complete passing result is visibly ready.
A visual or functional defect is visibly failed and names its affected state.
A missing required browser result is visibly incomplete and cannot be mistaken for ready.
The summary and each category expose enough evidence to explain the aggregate state.
The result is explicitly evidence about readiness, not approval or broader assurance.

sections.title: The browser support matrix needs an authoritative owner
sections.summary: Cross-browser readiness has no testable boundary until mandatory versions and platforms are declared.

blocks.question: Who declares the mandatory browser, version, and platform matrix for a report?

options.label: A repository-maintained matrix applies to every report in that repository
Each report author declares the matrix for that artifact
A shared baseline applies unless a repository explicitly overrides it
